scope: Three selected cases in research-batch-2c.json: two Sheahan cases and Patton's Gercone case.
method: Read the full extracted text of each actual official PDF, including covers, procedural history, reasoning, disposition and footnotes. Re-read tool-truncated portions separately. Matched the local PDF SHA-256 to the ledger. Compared judge attribution, trial action, reviewing outcome, date and pinpoint references against the ledger. No source ledgers edited by this reviewer.

cases.case: Glorioso v. Sun-Times Media Holdings, LLC
cases.result: Pass after later-law context added by source owner.
cases.verification: Cover identifies Sheahan; paragraphs 27-29 describe the first motion; paragraphs 41-42 identify the October 29, 2021 anti-SLAPP ruling and its rationale. Paragraphs 44-47 describe appellate affirmance and dissent. Paragraphs 67-80 establish the Supreme Court's objective first-prong inquiry and affirmance/remand. Footnote 6 rejects the appellate fact-question characterization without reversing its judgment. No final defamation liability or Trump tax ruling was attributed to Sheahan.
cases.finding: Core historical summary was accurate. Explicit later-law context was needed to avoid treating the 2024 press-protection rule as the current general rule for new actions.
cases.resolution: Owner added Public Act 104-0431, its August 21, 2025 effective date, express press protection and changed motive/sole-basis provisions, and limitation to actions commenced on or after January 1, 2026. This addition and primary source were re-read in the component ledger after the patch.

additionalSources.pinpoint: Section 5 amending 735 ILCS 110/5 and /15; new section 32; section 99 and effective-date line
additionalSources.readMethod: Official indexed full statutory text returned by web search. Direct opening returned 502; direct PDF download returned 403. No blocked response was treated as source text.

additionalSources.title: Anderson v. Smith, 2026 IL 131714
additionalSources.finding: Confirms the later statute's temporal limit. Separately clarifies the second-prong test for older cases; it explicitly notes that Glorioso decided the first prong and did not reach the second. This is not a reversal of Glorioso.

cases.case: Clanton v. Oakbrook Healthcare Centre, Ltd.
cases.verification: Cover identifies Sheahan and September 21, 2023 decision. Paragraph 8 describes substantive unconscionability of the damages limitation, rejection of waiver/procedural unconscionability, and refusal to sever. Paragraphs 10-11 distinguish the appellate termination-on-death reasoning. Paragraphs 25, 32-38 establish the Supreme Court's contract-interpretation ground and express rejection of contrary Mason reasoning. Paragraphs 39-40 affirm and remand. The summary correctly distinguishes forum selection from underlying negligence liability.

cases.case: Gercone v. Cook County Officers Electoral Board
cases.verification: Cover identifies Patton, June 8, 2022 filing and Rule 23 status. Paragraphs 3 and 16 establish her May 23, 2022 order restoring the candidate and rejecting the constitutional challenge; paragraph 16 supports the improper-delegation rationale. Paragraphs 28-40 support the appellate certificate-at-filing and agency-authority holdings. Paragraphs 41-65 separately address constitutional arguments, including forfeiture where applicable. Paragraphs 66-68 reverse the circuit judgment and affirm the electoral board. The ledger does not attribute appellate constitutional analysis or a party preference to Patton.

limitations: This verifies the historical rulings described in the selected official opinions, not a complete current docket, later remand history, or citator report.
The PDFs were read through their complete text layers; no new visual-layout claim is made.
No personal partisan orientation or Trump loyalty follows from these three records.
